correctness.rationale: Re-audit of the complete corrected RESULT.md in repairs/4: the theorem is unchanged. The frozen proof incorrectly claimed that with bridge triangle {x,y,z}, y in T and z outside T, the two y-layer special triples had Johnson distance at least two. For n=7, x=1, S={2,3,4}, T={5,6,7}, y=5, z=2, the bridge-side {1,2,6} and goal-side {1,6,7} are at distance one. The corrected proof requires only distance at least one: disjoint mandatory pairs {x,z} and T minus {y} cannot fit together in one triple. Since the x-side also needs to insert y into S, at least two Johnson moves in total are still necessary. If z lies in T, both y and z must be inserted on the x-side. Any path of length at most four to A(T) needs a two-edge change of center to a center in T plus its final edge; it can therefore use at most one Johnson move, a contradiction. Between disjoint triangles at most four steps would either use a single common center or an intermediate triangle sharing two elements with each endpoint, both impossible. For the upper bound within a center use Johnson distance at most three; between centers insert one desired center into the starting special triple, bridge through the triangle formed with a retained point, then choose a special triple meeting the target so at most two Johnson moves remain. The triangle-to-triangle and mixed routes give at most five using the exact adjacency rules. Inclusion–exclusion on pairs in a fixed center layer gives the stated same-center and mixed overlaps; direct bounds for distinct centers and triangle pairs are all strict below 2n-4. The equality types from Hilton–Milner exhaust the vertices even at n=7; the two equality overlap cases give degree 3(n-3), and label count plus handshaking give both totals. Independently replayed n=7 from the defining triple families in branches/1f1f1d1b-ae1a-4c4b-89bf-5cf3ec32458b/n7_hilton_milner_exchange_check.py and its .out: minimum exchange 3, 175 vertices, 630 fixed-center edges, 420 mixed edges, no other edges, and all 175 eccentricities 5. This finite replay does not replace the corrected all-n path and overlap proof. Frozen evidence was preserved.

value.rationale: The quantitative contrast is substantive: every nontrivial optimal state is isolated until exchanges grow linearly in n, yet the first admissible graph is regular and every vertex has maximum distance exactly five. The Johnson-layer and triangle-incidence rules explain this jump and give explicit transformations, beyond the classification of isolated extremizers. The repaired proof preserves this interpretation.
